newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks close off in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks close off in thin trade.

text.p: Caracas stocks closed off as large cross trades in utility Electricidad de Caracas and Corimon B dominated an otherwise thin session ahead of the long weekend's carnival holidays, traders said.
"We'll have to wait until Wednesday, after carnival, to see the bolsa react again," said Bancaracas broker Ricardo Larrazabal.
The market's leading index fell 0.53 percent to end at 6,393.36 points as nearly 24 million shares traded worth four billion bolivars ($8.4 million).
Foods company Mavesa pared mid-morning losses, closing off 3.25 bolivars at 157.75 following an early selloff on talk of a legal suit that might delist the stock.

"I don't think the claim, which runs to six billion bolivars, has much weight," said one broker who bought the stock in its dips. The claim follows a 1996 suit filed by food company Vinagres Coronoa after Mavesa broke its distribution contract.
However, "One never knows what will happen with all the judicial insecurity that exists in the country," said another broker who closed-out his position in Mavesa.
Nearly eight million Corimon B shares cross-traded, with the stock closing off 0.25 bolivars at 9.10. Electricidad closed down 1.50 bolivars at 495.50 as 3.5 million shares cross-traded.
Among total traded issues, 25 fell, 11 rose and four closed flat.
